questions.explanation: (A), (C) and (B) all reduce payload size — request count and payload size are separate levers on load time.

questions.topic: Load times, PWAs, accessibility and SQL
questions.stem: A CDN reduces latency because:
options: Cached copies sit physically closer to the user, shortening the round trip
It compresses content more aggressively
It removes the need for DNS lookup
It increases the server's bandwidth
questions.explanation: The mechanism is the mark — physical distance and round trips are what latency measures.

questions.topic: Load times, PWAs, accessibility and SQL
questions.stem: loading="lazy" on an image tag:
options: Defers downloading until the user scrolls near it
Compresses the image on the server
Loads the image before the rest of the page
Converts the image to a modern format
questions.explanation: The initial load therefore fetches only what is visible — stating that consequence is what earns the mark.

questions.topic: Load times, PWAs, accessibility and SQL
questions.stem: Which pair addresses latency rather than bandwidth?
options: A CDN and HTTP/2 multiplexing
Image compression and minification
Gzip and code splitting
WebP conversion and CSS purging
questions.explanation: Bandwidth is how much can flow; latency is the delay before it starts. Matching the fix to the constraint is the analytical move.

questions.topic: Load times, PWAs, accessibility and SQL
questions.stem: A question asking how to minimise load times wants:
options: Techniques that reduce it, with the mechanism for each
Methods of measuring load time in the Network tab
A comparison of browser performance
An analysis of bandwidth costs
questions.explanation: 2025 marker feedback specifically penalised answers describing how to investigate load time when asked how to reduce it.

questions.topic: Load times, PWAs, accessibility and SQL
questions.stem: defer differs from async on a script tag because defer:
options: Blocks rendering until the script executes
Prevents the script from loading at all
Preserves execution order and waits until parsing completes
Loads the script before the HTML
questions.explanation: Both avoid render-blocking; async executes as soon as it arrives, which can reorder dependent scripts.

questions.topic: Load times, PWAs, accessibility and SQL
questions.stem: Code splitting improves perceived performance by:
options: Compressing the JavaScript bundle
Deferring all scripts to the end of the body
Caching the bundle in local storage
Breaking a large bundle so only the code needed for the current view is downloaded
questions.explanation: It reduces the initial payload rather than the total, which is why it improves time to interactive specifically.

questions.topic: Load times, PWAs, accessibility and SQL
questions.stem: Which two files are required for a website to qualify as a PWA?
options: A manifest and a stylesheet
A service worker and a database schema
A service worker and a web app manifest
A manifest and a robots.txt
questions.explanation: The service worker provides offline capability, background operation and push; the manifest enables installation.

questions.topic: Load times, PWAs, accessibility and SQL
questions.stem: The web app manifest is written in:
options: JSON
XML
YAML
HTML
questions.explanation: JSON — It declares name, icons, colours and launch behaviour, and can define share-target and file-handling behaviour.

questions.topic: Load times, PWAs, accessibility and SQL
questions.stem: A service worker can respond to a request when the device is offline because it:
options: Runs on the server and caches responses there
Stores the entire site in local storage
Intercepts network requests and can serve cached files
Maintains an open connection to the server
questions.explanation: It runs in the browser as a background script separate from the page, which is also why it can handle push notifications.

questions.topic: Load times, PWAs, accessibility and SQL
questions.stem: A PWA still requires a browser engine because it:
options: Uses the vendor's native SDK
Cannot be installed to the home screen
Is built with web platform technologies and remains technically a website
Cannot access device APIs
questions.explanation: Its advantage is precisely that — a single codebase with web distribution, plus installability and offline capability.

questions.topic: Load times, PWAs, accessibility and SQL
questions.stem: Progressive enhancement requires that an unsupported advanced API:
options: Causes the page to display an error and stop
Be polyfilled in every case
Be feature-detected, with a fallback or clear message provided
Prevent the page from loading on older browsers
questions.explanation: The Background Sync example — telling the user the message could not be sent — is the canonical illustration.

questions.topic: Load times, PWAs, accessibility and SQL
questions.stem: A platform-specific app's distinguishing characteristics are:
options: Written in HTML and CSS, distributed via a URL
Installable but not offline-capable
Built with the vendor's SDK for one OS and distributed through that vendor's store
Requires a browser engine to run
questions.explanation: Its benefits — icon access, offline and background operation, OS integration, store presence — are the gaps PWAs were designed to close.

questions.topic: Load times, PWAs, accessibility and SQL
questions.stem: Which accessibility measure most directly helps a screen-reader user?
options: High colour contrast
Larger touch targets
Semantic HTML elements and alt text
Reduced animation
questions.explanation: Contrast helps low-vision users, touch targets help motor impairment and reduced animation helps vestibular sensitivity — each measure maps to a different need.

questions.topic: Load times, PWAs, accessibility and SQL
questions.stem: The strongest argument that accessibility benefits everyone is:
options: Accessible sites rank higher in search results
Clear labels reduce errors for all users, keyboard operation is faster for frequent users, and high contrast helps anyone in bright sunlight
Accessibility is legally required
Accessible sites load faster
questions.explanation: This is the point that lifts an extended accessibility answer from a list of tips to an argument.

questions.topic: Load times, PWAs, accessibility and SQL
questions.stem: Which SQL clause is applied last in the logical order of a query?
options: WHERE
GROUP BY
ORDER BY
FROM
questions.explanation: ORDER BY — Filtering and grouping shape the result set; sorting arranges the final output.

questions.topic: Load times, PWAs, accessibility and SQL
questions.stem: SELECT * FROM Products WHERE Price > 50 AND Category = 'Tools'; returns products:
options: Over $50 and in Tools
Over $50 or in Tools
In Tools regardless of price
Over $50 in any category
questions.explanation: AND requires both conditions — replacing it with OR produces (B), which is the standard near-miss.

questions.topic: Load times, PWAs, accessibility and SQL
questions.stem: Which query correctly counts customers per country, highest first?
options: SELECT Country, COUNT() FROM Customers ORDER BY COUNT() DESC;
SELECT Country FROM Customers GROUP BY COUNT(*);
SELECT DISTINCT Country FROM Customers ORDER BY Country DESC;
SELECT Country, COUNT() FROM Customers GROUP BY Country ORDER BY COUNT() DESC;
questions.explanation: (A) omits GROUP BY, which is required whenever a non-aggregated column accompanies an aggregate.

questions.topic: Load times, PWAs, accessibility and SQL
questions.stem: Joining four tables in a WHERE clause requires how many join conditions?
options: Two
Three
Four
One
questions.explanation: Three — Joining n tables requires n − 1 conditions, all connected with AND.

questions.topic: Load times, PWAs, accessibility and SQL
questions.stem: Dot notation becomes necessary when:
options: A query uses an aggregate function
More than one table is involved and column names could be ambiguous
The query includes an ORDER BY clause
String values are compared
questions.explanation: Once two tables are in play, use it on every field name — partial use is where ambiguity errors creep in.

questions.topic: Load times, PWAs, accessibility and SQL
questions.stem: UPDATE students SET grade = 95; executed without a WHERE clause will:
options: Set every student's grade to 95
Fail with a syntax error
Update only the first row
Create a new column
questions.explanation: It is syntactically valid and catastrophic — which is why "never UPDATE or DELETE without WHERE" is a standing rule.

questions.topic: Load times, PWAs, accessibility and SQL
questions.stem: Which is an aggregate function used with GROUP BY?
options: LIKE
DISTINCT
SUM()
JOIN
questions.explanation: The examinable set is MIN(), MAX(), COUNT(), SUM() and AVG().

questions.topic: Load times, PWAs, accessibility and SQL
questions.stem: WHERE CustomerName LIKE '%son' matches names that:
options: Begin with "son"
End with "son"
Contain "son" anywhere
Are exactly "son"
questions.explanation: The % wildcard precedes the literal, so any characters may come before it — 'son%' would produce (A).

questions.stem: A PWA queues journal entries written offline and sends them on reconnection. The mechanism is:
options: The web app manifest
The viewport meta tag
Local storage polling
A service worker, potentially using the Background Sync API
questions.explanation: Where Background Sync is unsupported, progressive enhancement requires telling the user the entry has not yet been sent.

questions.stem: A comment field renders user HTML directly into the DOM. The vulnerability and fix are:
options: XSS; sanitise before insertion with a library such as DOMPurify, plus output encoding and CSP
SQL injection; parameterised queries
CSRF; SameSite cookies
Broken authentication; MFA
questions.explanation: A verification method worth naming: inject a script tag and confirm it is stored and rendered as inert text.

questions.stem: A site loads in 11 seconds on a rural 4G connection. The highest-value first change is usually:
options: Adding a service worker
Adding more analytics
Reducing total bytes — compressing images and removing unused CSS and JavaScript
Increasing server RAM
questions.explanation: On a bandwidth-constrained link, payload dominates. On a distant but fast link, latency dominates and a CDN matters more.

questions.stem: A developer stores a JWT in localStorage for convenience. The security consequence is:
options: The token is sent with every request automatically
The token cannot be validated by the server
The token is exposed to any XSS flaw on the page
The token expires when the tab closes
questions.explanation: An HttpOnly cookie is not reachable from JavaScript, which is why session identifiers generally belong there.

questions.stem: Two teams disagree about an API's response shape mid-project. The preventive practice is:
options: Agreeing the data contract early, so both sides can build in parallel against a stub
Merging the two teams
Switching to a monolithic architecture
Delaying front-end work until the back end is complete
questions.explanation: Clarifying the data contract is the key named benefit of front-end/back-end collaboration.

questions.stem: Shell scripting contributes to a web workflow as:
options: A client-side scripting language for interactivity
A database query language
A styling mechanism for terminal output
Automation of repeatable build, test, deploy and backup sequences
questions.explanation: It is the manual ancestor of a CI/CD pipeline — the same steps, triggered by a person rather than by a commit.

questions.stem: A page works in Chrome but a CSS feature fails in Safari. The most appropriate response is:
options: Instruct users to switch browsers
Serve a different page to Safari users
Remove the feature entirely
Feature-detect and provide a fallback, adding vendor prefixes where required, and test across browsers
questions.explanation: It is progressive enhancement applied to CSS — baseline for everyone, best experience where supported.

questions.stem: An SSL certificate has expired. The immediate user-facing consequence is:
options: The site becomes unreachable at the network level
Data is transmitted unencrypted without any indication
The browser warns of an insecure connection, which trains users to dismiss warnings
DNS resolution fails
questions.explanation: The connection can still be encrypted, but identity can no longer be verified — and normalised warning dismissal is the deeper harm.

questions.stem: For a public-facing site with a small team and no offline requirement, the most defensible choice is:
options: A platform-specific app for each OS
A CMS with no custom development
A PWA built from the outset regardless of need
A responsive website, adding PWA capabilities only if a genuine offline or installability need emerges
questions.explanation: Justify from the requirement, not the technology — adding a service worker without an offline need adds cache-invalidation complexity for nothing.

questions.stem: An INSERT succeeds but SELECT ... WHERE Suburb = Newtown returns nothing. The fault is:
options: A missing index on the Suburb column
The connection is read-only
The table has no primary key
The string literal is unquoted, so Newtown is parsed as a column name
questions.explanation: Missing quotation marks around SQL string values was explicitly named in 2025 marker feedback.

questions.stem: Which is the strongest justification for a CDN on a school PWA used across a region?
options: It improves the site's search ranking
Cached static assets served from a nearer edge reduce latency for users far from the origin server
It removes the need for a service worker
It encrypts traffic end to end
questions.explanation: For a service worker caching the same assets, the CDN mainly helps the first visit — which is a nuance worth stating.

questions.stem: A dashboard page issues 240 separate HTTP requests. The most direct remedy is:
options: Increasing server memory
Combining and code-splitting assets, lazy-loading below-the-fold content, and using HTTP/2 multiplexing
Adding a service worker
Switching to a NoSQL database
questions.explanation: Request count is its own cost independent of total bytes, particularly on high-latency connections.

questions.stem: A form field indicates errors using red borders only. The accessibility failure is:
options: Insufficient contrast on the border colour
Missing viewport meta tag
Meaning conveyed by colour alone, with no text or programmatic association to the field
Excessive use of semantic elements
questions.explanation: Add a text message, an icon, and an association so assistive technology announces the error with the field.

questions.stem: Which best justifies choosing a relational database for a booking system?
options: The data is highly structured with strong relationships and integrity requirements between bookings, customers and resources
Relational databases scale horizontally more easily
Relational databases handle unstructured data better
Relational databases require no schema design
questions.explanation: (B) and (C) describe NoSQL strengths — matching the model to the data shape is the justification required.

questions.stem: A team wants to add a feature without destabilising the live site. The correct practice is:
options: Edit files directly on the production server outside business hours
Maintain a second copy of the folder as a backup
Comment out the previous implementation in place
Branch, develop and test in isolation, then merge after review
questions.explanation: Small, frequent commits and short-lived branches also minimise the chance of a painful merge conflict.

questions.stem: A CMS site is repeatedly compromised through plugins. The structural response is:
options: Abandon the CMS entirely
Disable all user accounts
Minimise the plugin footprint, use maintained plugins only, patch promptly and monitor
Move the site to HTTP to simplify configuration
questions.explanation: The CMS trade-off includes inheriting the security posture of every third-party component installed.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the trade-off involved in caching?
options: Caching trades freshness for speed, so the policy must match how often the resource changes
Caching always serves the freshest content available
Caching applies only to images and stylesheets
Caching eliminates the need for a CDN
questions.explanation: Versioned filenames allow aggressive caching of static assets while dynamic data stays current.

questions.stem: A login form posts over HTTP on public Wi-Fi. The attack enabled is:
options: SQL injection
A race condition
Man-in-the-middle interception of credentials
Path traversal
questions.explanation: TLS defeats it twice — encryption stops eavesdropping and the certificate stops impersonation.

questions.stem: Evidence of veracity problems in a dataset feeding a web dashboard would be:
options: The dataset is very large
Missing values, inconsistent formats and records contradicting an independent source
The data arrives every second
The data is stored as JSON
questions.explanation: Volume, velocity and variety describe the dataset's shape; veracity describes whether it can be trusted.

questions.stem: A Console error reads Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of null. The most likely cause is:
options: The database rejected the query
The script ran before the element existed in the DOM
The CSS file failed to load
The server returned a 500 error
questions.explanation: null means the lookup found nothing — usually a timing or selector problem, fixed with defer or a DOMContentLoaded handler.

questions.stem: Which best distinguishes bandwidth from latency?
options: Bandwidth is the delay before transfer begins
Bandwidth is capacity per unit time; latency is the delay before transfer begins
They measure the same property at different scales
Latency applies only to video streaming
questions.explanation: The distinction determines which optimisation will actually help — compression for bandwidth, CDN and multiplexing for latency.

questions.stem: Which is the strongest reason a PWA must be served over HTTPS?
options: It improves search ranking
Service workers require a secure context, since a worker intercepting all requests over an interceptable connection would be catastrophic
HTTPS is required by WCAG
HTTPS reduces load times
questions.explanation: Powerful APIs are gated behind HTTPS precisely because of their abuse potential.

questions.stem: A team must present a solution to a non-technical client. The most effective approach is:
options: Walk through the source code and database schema
Lead with the outcome against the client's stated criteria, use visuals, and avoid unexplained jargon
Provide the full technical documentation set
Demonstrate every feature in sequence
questions.explanation: Matching the artefact and vocabulary to the audience is the assessable skill here.

questions.stem: Which pairing of protocol and function is correct?
options: DNS transfers files; FTP resolves names
HTTPS resolves names; DNS encrypts traffic
POP3 sends mail; SMTP receives it
SMTP sends mail; IMAP syncs mail on the server; DNS resolves names to addresses
questions.explanation: SMTP 25 send-only, IMAP 143 sync and keep, POP3 110 download and remove, DNS 53 resolution.

questions.stem: The strongest concluding judgement in an 8-mark web question:
options: "The website functions correctly and looks professional."
"PWAs are generally superior to conventional websites."

"Judged on load performance, accessibility and offline reliability, the PWA meets its purpose — 1.6 s first contentful paint via lazy loading and a CDN, WCAG AA contrast and full keyboard operation, and offline journal entry through the service worker — though push notifications remain unsupported on some browsers, so the design feature-detects and degrades gracefully."
"The solution uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript and a Flask back end."
questions.explanation: Criteria, measured evidence, a named limitation with its mitigation, and a judgement tied to the specific solution.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: Which best explains why a PWA is preferred over separate iOS and Android apps for a small team?
options: PWAs have deeper access to device hardware
PWAs cannot be installed, reducing support burden
A single codebase serves all platforms and is distributed via the web, avoiding two builds and two store processes
PWAs are faster than native code in every case
questions.explanation: Platform-specific apps retain deeper OS integration — (A) is the trade-off being accepted, not a PWA advantage.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: A page's first load is fast but subsequent navigation is slow. The most likely missing technique is:
options: Image compression
Caching, so previously fetched resources are not re-downloaded
Minification of the initial bundle
A viewport meta tag
questions.explanation: Compression and minification help the first load; caching and service workers help every load after it.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: Which statement about HttpOnly cookies is correct?
options: They cannot be read by JavaScript, limiting the impact of XSS
They cannot be sent over HTTP
They expire when the browser closes
They are never sent on cross-site requests
questions.explanation: Secure does (B), a session cookie does (C) and SameSite does (D) — four behaviours, four attributes.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: A team stores all site content in a database and renders it with a template engine. The primary benefit is:
options: Faster page loads than static HTML
Improved accessibility conformance
Content can change without editing markup, and one template serves many records
Reduced need for version control
questions.explanation: Content can change without touching markup, and one template serves many records — which is why CMS platforms exist. Static HTML is usually faster, so the speed claim is the trap.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: Which is the strongest reason to use semantic HTML rather than generic containers?
options: Semantic elements render faster
They convey document structure to assistive technology and to search engines
They require less CSS
They are required by HTTP/2
questions.explanation: A <div> soup is visually identical and structurally meaningless to a screen-reader user.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: A developer applies styling with inline style attributes throughout a 30-page site. The main consequence is:
options: Every change must be repeated on every element, and the styles cannot be cached
The pages will not validate
The site cannot be made responsive
Specificity conflicts are eliminated
questions.explanation: Inline styles also win specificity battles, making later overrides painful — which is why they are discouraged.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: SELECT Name FROM Staff WHERE Dept = 'IT' OR Dept = 'HR' ORDER BY Name; returns:
options: Staff in IT only, sorted by name
Staff in both IT and HR simultaneously
Staff in either IT or HR, sorted by name ascending
An error, since OR cannot be used with ORDER BY
questions.explanation: ORDER BY defaults to ascending. (B) misreads OR as requiring both, which no single-value field could satisfy.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: Which is the correct way to count how many products cost more than $100?
options: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Products GROUP BY Price > 100;
SELECT COUNT(Price > 100) FROM Products;
SELECT Price FROM Products WHERE COUNT(*) > 100;
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Products WHERE Price > 100;
questions.explanation: Filter with WHERE, then aggregate. (C) misuses an aggregate inside WHERE, which requires HAVING after grouping.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: A three-table join returns far more rows than expected. The most likely cause is:
options: An incorrect ORDER BY clause
Unquoted string literals
An aggregate without GROUP BY
A missing join condition, producing a partial Cartesian product
questions.explanation: Joining n tables requires n − 1 conditions — omitting one multiplies the result set rather than raising an error.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: Which SQL statement risks the greatest accidental damage?
options: SELECT * FROM Orders;
DELETE FROM Orders;
INSERT INTO Orders (id) VALUES (1);
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Orders;
questions.explanation: Without a WHERE clause it removes every row, and it is syntactically valid — which is what makes the omission so dangerous.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: An ORM is described as reducing SQL injection risk because it:
options: Generates parameterised queries by default rather than concatenating strings
Encrypts query parameters
Restricts queries to read-only operations
Validates all user input automatically
questions.explanation: Raw-SQL escape hatches in most ORMs reintroduce the risk, so the protection is a default rather than a guarantee.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: A team chooses MongoDB for a system with strictly relational booking data and heavy reporting joins. The best critique is:
options: MongoDB cannot store dates
MongoDB cannot be hosted in Australia
NoSQL databases cannot scale
The data shape and access pattern favour a relational model with enforced integrity and native joins
questions.explanation: Match the model to the data. NoSQL's flexible schema and horizontal scaling are not advantages for this workload.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: Which measure most directly improves time to interactive rather than total download size?
options: Compressing images
Code splitting so only the current view's JavaScript is parsed and executed
Enabling gzip on the server
Converting images to WebP
questions.explanation: Parse and execute cost is separate from transfer cost — a small but complex bundle can still block interactivity.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: A service worker caches an old version of the site and users see stale content. The required practice is:
options: A cache versioning and invalidation strategy, with the worker updating on new deployments
Removing the service worker entirely
Increasing the cache size limit
Disabling HTTPS during deployment
questions.explanation: Cache invalidation is the characteristic cost of adding a service worker — which is why one should not be added without an offline need.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: Which is the strongest evidence that a site is keyboard accessible?
options: All interactive elements have hover styles
The colour contrast meets AA
The site uses semantic HTML
Every control can be reached and operated by keyboard alone, with a visible focus indicator and logical order
questions.explanation: Semantic HTML supports it and contrast is a different criterion — the test is actual operability without a pointer.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: A form's error summary appears visually but is not announced by a screen reader. The likely omission is:
options: Sufficient colour contrast
A larger font size
A programmatic association and live-region announcement linking the error to the field
A submit button label
questions.explanation: Visual presence is not the same as programmatic exposure — this is the "robust" principle in WCAG's POUR.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: An enterprise wants its site indexed accurately by search engines and assistants. The relevant W3C work is:
options: Machine-readable data — RDF, JSON-LD and Schema.org
WAI and WCAG
Internationalisation
Web security
questions.explanation: Structured data lets a machine interpret what a page is about rather than merely what words it contains.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: Which is the most accurate statement about HTTPS and SEO or performance claims?
options: HTTPS slows page loads significantly
HTTPS prevents caching
HTTPS is required for service workers and other powerful APIs, and modern TLS costs little in performance
HTTPS removes the need for input validation
questions.explanation: (D) is the dangerous misconception — transport security says nothing about what the application does with the data.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: A back-end route returns 500 errors under load but works in testing. The most useful first diagnostic is:
options: The browser Console
Server logs and the Network tab's response detail, then load testing to reproduce
The Elements panel
The CSS specificity chain
questions.explanation: A 500 is generated server-side, so the client-side panels can only show the symptom.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: Which best describes the role of a data contract between front and back end?
options: A legal agreement between the two teams
The authentication scheme used by the API
The database schema shared with the front end
The agreed shape of the data an API sends and receives, allowing both sides to build in parallel
questions.explanation: Agreeing it early is the key named benefit of front-end/back-end collaboration.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: A team adds a CDN but the site is still slow for local users on a fast connection. The likely explanation is:
options: The CDN is misconfigured
The CDN cannot serve dynamic content
The bottleneck is payload size or render-blocking scripts rather than latency
HTTPS is adding overhead
questions.explanation: Diagnose the constraint before selecting the fix — a CDN addresses distance, not bytes or blocking.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: Which is the best reason to keep a website's JavaScript optional for core content?
options: JavaScript is insecure
JavaScript cannot be minified
Search engines cannot execute JavaScript at all
Progressive enhancement — content remains available when scripts fail, are blocked or load slowly
questions.explanation: Baseline for everyone, best experience for capable browsers — and script failure is more common than it appears.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: A shared hosting account exposes /config.php containing database credentials. The failure is:
options: Security misconfiguration — sensitive files served from the webroot without protection
Insufficient TLS configuration
Broken authentication
An SQL injection vulnerability
questions.explanation: Configuration and secrets belong outside the webroot or in environment-provided values, never in a served path.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: Which practice most reduces the risk of a merge conflict?
options: Committing once at the end of each feature
Working directly on the main branch
Small, frequent commits on short-lived branches, merged often
Disabling branch protection rules
questions.explanation: (B) removes conflicts by removing isolation, at the cost of stability — which is not a trade worth making.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: A CMS plugin adds 400 KB of JavaScript to every page for a feature used on one page. The best response is:
options: Accept it, since plugins are pre-tested
Load the plugin conditionally on the page that needs it, or replace it with a lighter approach
Minify the plugin's code
Increase the server's bandwidth allocation
questions.explanation: Conditional loading addresses the cause; minification (C) trims the symptom.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: Which is the strongest justification for choosing a CMS for a school's public site?
options: It offers the greatest technical flexibility
It guarantees better security than a custom build
Non-technical staff must publish content regularly without developer involvement
It removes the need for hosting
questions.explanation: Justify from who maintains the content — the trade-off is less granular control and inherited plugin risk.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: A site's images are served at 4000 px wide and displayed at 400 px. The remedy is:
options: Lazy loading only
Deferring the image scripts
Adding a CDN
Serving appropriately sized responsive images, with compression and a modern format
questions.explanation: Lazy loading defers the cost; right-sizing removes it — and a CDN would simply deliver oversized files faster.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: A developer must debug why a button click does nothing. The most efficient first step is:
options: Inspect the CSS specificity chain
Test the site in a different browser
Review the server logs
Check the Console for errors and confirm the event listener is attached in the Sources or Elements panel
questions.explanation: Console errors resolve a large share of these cases immediately, and listener attachment is the next most common cause.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: Which best describes the purpose of a robots.txt file?
options: It advises compliant crawlers which paths not to request
It enforces access control on private pages
It encrypts pages from search engines
It prevents users from viewing page source
questions.explanation: It is advisory, not a security control — listing a sensitive path in it advertises that path to anyone who looks.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: A team wants offline access, installability and push notifications on a budget. The best recommendation is:
options: Two platform-specific apps
A responsive website with no additional capability
A PWA with a service worker and manifest
A desktop application
questions.explanation: All three requirements are exactly what the PWA capabilities provide from a single codebase.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: Which is the most accurate description of async on a script tag?
options: The script executes only after the document has fully parsed
The script is never executed
The script downloads in parallel and executes as soon as it is ready, which may reorder dependent scripts
The script blocks rendering until complete
questions.explanation: defer preserves order and waits for parsing — choosing between them depends on whether order matters.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: An API returns 200 OK with an error message in the body. The problem is:
options: The response is too large
The body cannot contain JSON
Clients relying on status codes will treat a failure as a success
200 responses cannot be cached
questions.explanation: Status codes are the machine-readable contract — misusing them pushes error handling into ad-hoc body parsing.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: Which statement about session storage in a PWA is correct?
options: It persists across browser restarts
It clears when the tab is closed, making it unsuitable for offline data that must survive a restart
It is sent to the server with each request
It is the only storage a service worker can access
questions.explanation: For durable offline data a service worker's cache or IndexedDB is appropriate.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: A developer hard-codes an API key into front-end JavaScript. The consequence is:
options: The key is fully visible to any user, so it must be treated as public
The key is obfuscated by minification
The key is protected by HTTPS in transit
The key can only be read by the same origin
questions.explanation: Anything shipped to the browser is public. Secrets belong on the server, with the front end calling a protected endpoint.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: Which best explains why the same page renders differently across browsers?
options: Different network protocols
Different HTTP status handling
Different DNS resolvers
Different rendering engines with differing standards support and default styles
questions.explanation: A CSS reset or normalise addresses default-style differences; feature detection addresses support differences.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: A form submits successfully but the record is not saved. The most useful diagnostic sequence is:
options: Check CSS, then HTML, then JavaScript
Check the Network tab for the request and its response, then the server logs and the database write
Clear the browser cache and retry
Rebuild the front-end bundle
questions.explanation: Follow the request through each layer rather than guessing — the failure could be client, transport, server or database.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: Which is the most defensible reason to add a service worker to an existing site?
options: Service workers are considered best practice
They reduce server bandwidth costs
They improve search ranking
A demonstrated need for offline access, background sync or push notifications
questions.explanation: Adding one without a need buys cache-invalidation complexity for no user benefit.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: An enterprise's API is rate limited at 10 requests per second per client. A legitimate integration is blocked. The best response is:
options: Remove rate limiting entirely
Provide a documented higher-tier key or batch endpoint, keeping the protection for anonymous callers
Whitelist the client's IP address permanently
Increase the global limit for all clients
questions.explanation: Differentiated limits preserve the DoS protection while accommodating a known, authenticated consumer.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: Which best describes the trade-off of server-side rendering versus client-side rendering?
options: Server-side rendering is always faster
They produce identical results in every respect
Client-side rendering is always more accessible
Server-side rendering improves first paint and works without JavaScript, at the cost of server load
questions.explanation: Client-side rendering shifts work to the device, improving subsequent navigation but delaying first meaningful content.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: A team must justify their choice of back-end framework. The strongest structure is:
options: Name the most popular framework in current use
List the features of the chosen framework
State the criteria — team skills, ecosystem fit, hosting, security features, maintainability — evaluate, and say why the alternatives are worse
Describe the framework's request lifecycle
questions.explanation: "Justify" requires rejecting alternatives — a feature list is description.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: Which is the strongest evidence a site meets its performance criteria?
options: It "feels fast" to the development team
The images have been compressed
It uses a CDN and caching
Measured metrics against stated targets on a representative connection and device
questions.explanation: Measurement against a defined target is what evaluation requires. A CDN, caching and image compression are techniques applied, not evidence that the criteria were met.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: A team's site works locally but fails when deployed. The most common cause category is:
options: Browser incompatibility
Environment differences — paths, environment variables, database connection and HTTPS configuration
Insufficient CSS specificity
Missing semantic HTML
questions.explanation: Which is why staging environments that mirror production exist, and why configuration belongs outside the code.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: Which is the best reason to validate input on both client and server?
options: Client validation is a security control and server validation is a usability feature
Client validation gives immediate feedback; server validation is the actual security boundary
Duplicate validation halves the error rate
Server validation cannot check formats
questions.explanation: (A) is the pair inverted — the client can always be bypassed, so it can never be the boundary.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: A team wants to reduce total requests without losing caching benefits. The best approach is:
options: Inline every asset into the HTML document
Disable caching to guarantee freshness
Serve every asset from a separate domain
Bundle related assets with versioned filenames, so they cache well and change together
questions.explanation: (A) makes everything uncacheable and re-downloaded on every page — the opposite of the intended effect.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: Which best describes the accessibility obligation for a CAPTCHA?
options: It must be solvable within 30 seconds
It must use only alphanumeric characters
An accessible alternative must be available for users who cannot complete the visual challenge
It must be served over HTTPS
questions.explanation: A load-protection control that locks out legitimate users has traded one failure for another.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: A page's contrast ratio is 3.8:1 for body text. The status is:
options: Non-compliant — AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text
Compliant with WCAG AA
Compliant with AAA
Compliant only for large text at AAA
questions.explanation: 3:1 is the AA minimum for large text; 7:1 is AAA for normal text.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: Which is the most defensible reason to use a front-end framework rather than plain JavaScript?
options: Frameworks are always faster at runtime
Frameworks guarantee accessibility
Frameworks remove the need for testing
The application has substantial state and component reuse that a framework manages more reliably than ad-hoc code
questions.explanation: A brochure site gains little and pays a bundle-size cost — justify from the application's complexity.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: A team documents its API with example requests and responses. The primary benefit is:
options: It replaces the need for automated tests
It improves the API's performance
Consumers can integrate without reading the implementation, and the data contract becomes explicit
It satisfies WCAG requirements
questions.explanation: Documentation is how the contract is communicated; tests are how it is enforced.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: Which best distinguishes a library from a framework in practice?
options: A framework is smaller and more focused
You call a library; a framework calls your code within a structure it defines
Libraries are only for the front end
Frameworks cannot be extended
questions.explanation: Inversion of control is the defining difference, and it is why framework choice constrains architecture more than library choice.

questions.topic: Mixed review — Programming for the Web
questions.stem: In an extended web response, the reliable way to earn marks is to:
options: Name as many technologies as possible
Provide code samples for each point
Explain the mechanism — why the technique produces the effect — and tie it to the specific solution in the stimulus
Compare the solution to commercial alternatives
questions.explanation: "A CDN reduces load time" earns little; "cached copies sit physically closer so latency falls" earns the mark.
